liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Reviewer recalls Jerry's chord leads in this song as jaw-dropping; Reviewer calls it the best of 1980 and among the best of the 80s or 90s [11][16]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer could not get through half of it because of the left channel fading [19]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer praises the Feel Like A Stranger, High Time, Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance stretch before drums [21]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Reviewer says the band rocked it out, far different from the radio version they knew [12]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Reviewer first heard this version of the song on nug.net, which led them to seek out the show [15]

## The recordings

- **gd80-09-03.aud.bass.16925.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 162 min; rated 3.87/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the audience recording very well done and good sounding throughout; Reviewer describes it as a good, balanced audience recording; A person clapping constantly near the microphones spoils the recording, especially during Althea and Let It Grow [10][13][17]
- **gd1980-09-03.aud.cribbs.12576.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 167 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Left channel repeatedly fades in and out, a problem in Franklin's Tower; the other copy has it too; Reviewer calls the Wise audience recording immaculate and says the audience was stoked [19][21]
- **gd1980-09-03.143031.aud.sterry.beckwith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 25 songs; 162 min [3]
- **gd1980-09-03.143030.aud.sterry.beckwith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 162 min [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended from the fourth row and taped the show, mostly capturing Jerry's amp or monitor, so the balance was uneven [11]
- The first four songs of the first set run straight into each other [11]
- Reviewer's first Dead concert; remembered lyrics of He's Gone and High Time, then bought Workingman's Dead and Europe 72 next day [12]
- Reviewer worked a odd job for the band that day, missed some songs, and remembers the show as well played [14]
- Reviewer says the first set stands out for especially high energy, song choices and playing [10]
- Reviewer rates the first set's power above the Radio City shows they saw weeks later, and above Rochester [16]
- Second set's intensity eases from breakneck to merely great [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-09-03.aud.bass.16925.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Lineage runs from a Mac through an unknown step to CD, then secure-mode EAC, encoded to seekable SHN v3; Charles Bass extracted the audio and encoded it to shorten files [1]
- **gd1980-09-03.aud.cribbs.12576.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise and Eddie Claridge; transferred by Sean Cribbs; source: Sony ECM-280 mics > Sony TC-D5 [2]
- **gd1980-09-03.143031.aud.sterry.beckwith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by George Sterry; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and David Beckwith; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Primary: George Sterry's Master Audience Cassettes; Unknown mics > Sony TC-158SD > 1st generation cassette (TDK D90); Secondary:… [3]
- **gd1980-09-03.143030.aud.sterry.beckwith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by George Sterry; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and David Beckwith; source: Source Info: Primary: George Sterry's Master Audience Cassettes; Unknown mics > Sony TC-158SD > 1st generation cassette (TDK D90); Secondary: George Sterry's… [4]
